skill.name: azure-mgmt-applicationinsights-dotnet
skill.description: Guidance for using the Azure.ResourceManager.ApplicationInsights .NET SDK to manage Application Insights resources, web tests, workbooks, API keys, and linked storage.
skill.summary: Manage Azure Application Insights resources with focused .NET SDK examples.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static findings were false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code, sample URLs, and documentation links. No prompt injection or hidden execution intent was found, but sample code exposes Application Insights secrets through console output.

remediation.issue: Sample code prints sensitive Application Insights values.
remediation.suggestion: Remove Console.WriteLine statements for connection strings and API keys. Show redacted output and recommend Key Vault or managed identity storage.

remediation.issue: Generated API key handling is unsafe in the example.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to copy the key directly into a secret store and never write it to logs, terminals, or telemetry.

semantic_findings.title: Secret Exposure in Sample Output
semantic_findings.description: The sample code prints the Application Insights connection string, instrumentation key, and generated API key to console. Users may copy this into production tooling and expose credentials in logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly writes connection strings, instrumentation keys, and API keys with Console.WriteLine. Generated API keys are sensitive and can leak through logs.

content.value_statement: Managing Application Insights resources with the .NET Azure SDK can require many object names and workflows. This skill gives focused examples for components, web tests, workbooks, API keys, and linked storage.
actual_capabilities: Shows package setup for Azure.ResourceManager.ApplicationInsights and Azure.Identity.
Explains DefaultAzureCredential authentication for Azure Resource Manager clients.
Provides .NET examples for creating workspace-based Application Insights components.
Demonstrates availability web tests, multi-step web tests, and workbook creation.
Covers API key creation, linked storage, listing, updating, and deleting resources.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not run Azure operations by itself.
Examples use placeholder resource names and subscription values.
It does not validate Azure permissions, quotas, or regional availability.
Users must check current SDK behavior against official Azure documentation.

use_cases.title: Provision observability resources
use_cases.description: Create workspace-based Application Insights components with tags, retention settings, ingestion settings, and linked Log Analytics workspaces.

use_cases.title: Build availability monitoring
use_cases.description: Use the SDK patterns to define URL ping tests and multi-step web tests across Azure test locations.

use_cases.title: Document monitoring workflows
use_cases.description: Prepare internal examples for workbooks, API keys, storage links, and component lifecycle operations.

prompt_templates.title: Start a component example
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to create a workspace-based Application Insights component with the Azure .NET SDK. Use placeholders for all resource IDs.

prompt_templates.title: Add availability tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a URL ping web test for Application Insights. Include frequency, timeout, retry behavior, and multiple Azure test locations.

prompt_templates.title: Create dashboard resources
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a .NET SDK workflow for creating an Application Insights workbook that charts request volume over time.

prompt_templates.title: Plan resource lifecycle automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a safe Application Insights resource management flow for create, list, update, and delete operations. Include secret handling guidance.

output_examples.input: Create a workspace-based Application Insights component.
output_examples.output: The response describes the needed Azure client, resource group lookup, component data settings, Log Analytics workspace link, tags, and create operation.

output_examples.input: Add a multi-step login availability test.
output_examples.output: The response outlines the web test type, endpoint placeholders, request sequence, test locations, frequency, timeout, and retry settings.

output_examples.input: Explain how to manage API keys safely.
output_examples.output: The response separates SDK key creation from secret storage and recommends redaction, restricted permissions, rotation, and secure vault storage.

best_practices: Replace all placeholders with reviewed resource IDs before deployment.
Store connection strings and API keys in a managed secret store.
Confirm SDK versions and Azure API behavior before production use.
anti_patterns: Do not log generated API keys, connection strings, or instrumentation keys.
Do not use sample domains or placeholder credentials in live tests.
Do not delete monitoring resources without a rollback and retention plan.

faq.question: Does this skill create Azure resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides reference guidance and examples for users or agents to adapt.

faq.question: Which SDK package does it cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on Azure.ResourceManager.ApplicationInsights for .NET resource management.

faq.question: Can it help with availability tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for URL ping tests and multi-step web tests.

faq.question: Does it cover telemetry instrumentation?
faq.answer: Only briefly. Its main focus is Azure resource management, not application telemetry code.

faq.question: Is it safe to copy the examples directly?
faq.answer: Review them first. Replace placeholders and remove any output that exposes secrets.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
